## Some Alt keys changed

In ZTreeWin, **Ctrl** and **Alt** mean two different things, and Xylem now
follows it:

- **Ctrl+letter** acts on the tagged files, as before: Ctrl+C copies them,
  Ctrl+D deletes them, Ctrl+T tags everything.
- **Alt+letter** is the other version of a command. In the tree it acts on
  the whole branch (Alt+P Prune, Alt+R Release); in the file window, on the
  tagged files keeping their paths (Alt+C, Alt+M); and it opens the tools
  (Alt+U Usage, Alt+D Duplicates, Alt+S Sort, Alt+X the terminal).

Up to 0.7, several Alt keys only repeated the Ctrl ones. These changed:

| Key | Up to 0.7 | From 0.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Alt+A | Attributes of the tagged files | nothing (use Ctrl+A) |
| Alt+D | delete the tagged files | **Duplicates** (to delete the tagged files: Ctrl+D) |
| Alt+R | rename the tagged files | **Release** the branch, the same as `-` (to rename the tagged files: Ctrl+R) |
| Alt+T | tag everything | nothing (use Ctrl+T) |
| Alt+U | untag everything | **Usage** (to untag everything: Ctrl+U) |
| Alt+W | Usage | nothing (use Alt+U) |
| Alt+Y | Duplicates | nothing (use Alt+D) |

**If you used Alt+D to delete the tagged files:** it now opens Duplicates,
which deletes nothing without asking first.

**To keep the old keys,** add them to `[keys.any]` in `config.toml`, one or
all of them. All of them, as they were up to 0.7:

```toml
[keys.any]
"alt+a" = "attributes_tagged"
"alt+d" = "delete_tagged"
"alt+r" = "rename_tagged"
"alt+t" = "tag_all"
"alt+u" = "untag_all"
"alt+w" = "usage"
"alt+y" = "duplicates"
```

They work in both windows, Alt+R in the tree included, and Release is still
on `-`. If you already set keys of your own in `[keys]`, those stay as you
set them. To see the keys in effect, press **K** in the help (F1).

The manual explains all this in "What Ctrl and Alt mean", on the tagging page.

## Every command is in a menu

Before, some commands worked but appeared in no menu. Now each one has its
place in the footer:

- **N** New date (Ctrl+N for the tagged files), **A** Available (in the tree),
  `?` statistics, `\` Treespec;
- F5 and Ctrl+F5 for archives, F7 Autoview, F12 setup;
- Ctrl+B Batch, Ctrl+S Search and Ctrl+V View of the tagged files;
- Ctrl+F7, Ctrl+F8 and Ctrl+F9 to tag, untag and invert the whole branch;
- Alt+Q to quit and leave the shell in the current folder.

For that, the footer usually takes **three lines** instead of two: the
commands by letter, in alphabetical order, on the first two, and the function
keys and symbols on the third. On a screen wide enough for every menu to fit,
it keeps **two lines**, so the tree loses no line there.

The menus also show only what works where you are. Inside an archive, they
leave out what would write to it. On a remote machine, they now show
everything that works there, including Delete, Makedir, Move, Rename,
Attributes and New date, which the old menu left out.

## Menus on a narrow screen

When a menu does not fit the width of the window, its words are first
shortened, all by the same amount and always keeping the highlighted letter.
Only if that is not enough do the last entries leave, with a `…` where they
were. F9 (or Esc) always stays.

## Smaller things

- **Several terminals side by side:** the manual now shows how to run tmux in
  the built-in terminal (Alt+X) and split it into panes. With tmux, the tree
  follows only the shell Xylem started, and the tmux session goes on after
  Xylem closes.
- **Seconds in the clock:** F12, page 2, **Q** (or `clock_seconds = true`).
  Off by default.
- **B in Branch or Showall** goes back to the folder's own list, instead of
  building the same Branch again.
- **The small file window** under the tree now takes a quarter of the screen's
  height, with at least 3 files: more files on a tall terminal, more tree on a
  short one. On an ordinary 34-line screen it looks as before.
- **The history of a prompt is a list:** ↑ opens it just above the line, with
  the last entry at the bottom. Typing filters it, Enter puts an entry in the
  line (another Enter confirms), Del takes it out for good and Esc closes it.
  ↓ no longer goes through the entries one by one; in the Batch of the viewer,
  PgUp opens the list.
- **Treespec (`/`):** Ctrl+← takes the last folder off the path, and Ctrl+→
  brings them back one by one.

## Install

Download the archive for your system below (Linux x86_64 or ARM64, static;
Windows x86_64), a `.deb` or `.rpm` package, or `cargo install xylem-fm`. The
website: https://andrelnfernandes.github.io/xylem/
